1	---
2	title: cacheComponents
3	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4	related:
5	  links:
6	    - app/getting-started/caching
7	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
29	
30	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
31	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
32	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
33	
34	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
35	
36	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
37	
38	Read [How rendering works](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#how-rendering-works) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
39	
40	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
41	
42	## Navigation with Activity
43	
44	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
45	
46	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
47	
48	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
49	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
50	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
51	
52	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
53	
54	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
55	
56	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
57	
58	## Version History
59	
60	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
61	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
62	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
63

...
48 } 49 ``` 50 51 ## `dynamic = "force-static"` 52 53 Start by removing it. When unhandled uncached or runtime data access is detected during development and build time, Next.js raises an error. Otherwise, the prerendering step automatically extracts the static HTML shell. 54 55 For uncached data access, add [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) as close to the data access as possible with a long [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) like `'max'` to maintain cached behavior. If needed, add it at the top of the page or layout. 56 57 For runtime data access (`cookies()`, `headers()`, etc.), errors will direct you to wrap it with ``. ...

...

...

...
100 } 101 ``` 102 103 ## `revalidate` 104 105 **Replace with `cacheLife`.** Use the `cacheLife` function to define cache duration instead of the route segment config. 106 107 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 108 // Before 109 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 110 111 export default async function Page() { 112 return

...

...

...
144 } 145 ``` 146 147 ## `fetchCache` 148 149 **Not needed.** With `use cache`, all data fetching within a cached scope is automatically cached, making `fetchCache` unnecessary. 150 151 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 152 // Before 153 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 154 ``` 155 156 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 157 // Before 158 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 159 ``` 160 161 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 162 // After - Use 'use cache' to control caching behavior 163 export default async function Page() { 164 'use cache' 165 // All fetches here are cached 166 return

Switch to the Node.js runtime (the default) by removing the [deprecated](/docs/messages/edge-runtime-deprecated) `runtime = 'edge'` export. If you need edge behavior for specific routes, use [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy) instead. 182 183 ## UI state preservation 184 185 **Component state now persists across navigations.** With Cache Components, Next.js preserves routes using React's [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component in [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity) mode instead of unmounting them. Effects clean up and re-run normally, but `useState` values, form inputs, and scroll position are no longer reset when navigating away and back. 186 187 If your code relied on unmounting to clear state, you may need to add explicit reset logic: 188 189 - **Dropdowns and popovers** — stay open when navigating back. Close them in a `useLayoutEffect` cleanup function. 190 - **Dialogs with initialization logic** — Effects that depend on dialog state (like focusing an input) won't re-fire if the state was preserved. Derive dialog state from the URL instead. 191 - **Forms after submission** — input values and `useActionState` results (success/error messages) persist when returning. Reset in the submit handler or user action when possible, otherwise use a cleanup effect. 192 193 See [Preserving UI state across navigations](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for detailed examples of each pattern. 194

events.content:
PPR is now enabled and working. The build confirms it: ``` Route (app) ┌ ◐ / ← Partial Prerender └ ○ /_not-found ◐ (Partial Prerender) prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content ``` ## What I did **The key insight:** This is Next.js 16, where PPR is no longer a standalone flag. The old `experimental.ppr` config and `experimental_ppr` route segment export have been **removed**. PPR is now delivered through the unified `cacheComponents` flag (per `node_modules/next/dist/docs/.../cacheComponents.md`), which also subsumes the former `dynamicIO` and `useCache` experimental flags. **The only change needed** was `next.config.ts`: ```ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } ``` **No code migration was required** because your `app/` was already structured perfectly for PPR: - `app/page.tsx` has a static shell (`

Store

`) with the two data-fetching components (`ProductList`, `Recommendations`) each wrapped in their own `` boundary. - Those components do uncached `fetch` calls, so under Cache Components they're dynamic by default and stream in — exactly the PPR model. The static shell prerenders; dynamic content streams within it. - There were no `dynamic`/`revalidate`/`fetchCache` route segment configs to migrate away from. ## Worth knowing `cacheComponents` brings two behaviors beyond PPR that may matter as you build out the app: 1. **Dynamic-by-default + `use cache`** — if you want any data actually *cached* (rather than re-fetched per request), add the `'use cache'` directive with `cacheLife()` at the page/component/function level. The build will error on unhandled uncached data access that isn't wrapped in `Suspense`. 2. **State preservation on navigation** — Next.js now keeps recent routes mounted via React `` in `"hidden"` mode rather than unmounting. `useState`, form inputs, and scroll position persist across back/forward navigation. If anything in the app relies on unmount-to-reset, see the "Preserving UI state" guide.
